approvalText: I approve the ME-11 five-candidate proposal exactly as written: actinomycosis -> osteomyelitis restricted to cervicofacial/oral actinomycosis with mandibular osteomyelitis (PMID 41871568); insomnia -> hypertension as population-level risk/association only with source replacement to PMID 33360604; periodontal-disease -> osteoporosis narrowed to periodontitis and association/risk only with source replacement to PMID 36377800; uterine-fibroids -> endometriosis as co-occurrence/association only with source replacement to PMID 31006843; and bronchiolitis -> pulmonary-hypertension restricted to post-lung-transplant bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome/chronic lung allograft dysfunction with separately diagnosed pulmonary hypertension (PMID 42444963). I approve all stated phenotype restrictions, confounder protections, treatment/transplant-context requirements, chronology boundaries, and publication guards. I authorize creation of a separate fail-closed local-only ME-11 implementation package for exactly these five relationships, with all five new references remaining verified:false and all five new master sources pending-verification. I do not authorize citation promotion or any GitHub/Vercel write.

rows.sourceTitle: Pediatric cervicofacial actinomycosis presenting with mandibular osteomyelitis: a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge and literature review
rows.proposition: Actinomycotic osteomyelitis is a rare chronic infection caused by Actinomyces species; mandibular involvement can occur in cervicofacial/oral actinomycosis.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: cervicofacial/oral actinomycosis with compatible mandibular involvement; target is mandibular osteomyelitis
rows.publicationGuard: Require clinically established cervicofacial/oral actinomycosis plus a separately diagnosed mandibular osteomyelitis phenotype. Do not generalize to all actinomycosis or all osteomyelitis. Preserve odontogenic infection, trauma, surgery, malignancy and other infectious causes. The source is rare-disease/case-plus-review evidence and must not be presented as population-level causal proof.
rows.citation: Yildirim Arslan S, Tigrak S, Yucel E, Demirci M, Ekici O. Pediatric cervicofacial actinomycosis presenting with mandibular osteomyelitis: a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge and literature review. Turk J Pediatr. 2026. PMID 41871568. doi:10.24953/turkjpediatr.2026.6451.

rows.sourceTitle: Insomnia and the risk of hypertension: A meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies
rows.proposition: Across 14 prospective cohorts involving 395,641 participants, insomnia was associated with increased incident hypertension risk (pooled RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10-1.33).
rows.phenotypeRestriction: independently established insomnia and separately diagnosed hypertension
rows.publicationGuard: Treat as population-level association/risk only, not individual causation. Evidence was stronger for difficulty maintaining sleep and early-morning awakening than for sleep-onset difficulty. Preserve obstructive sleep apnea, obesity, age, sex, renal/endocrine disease, medications/substances, sleep duration and other conventional hypertension risks.
rows.citation: Li L, Gan Y, Zhou X, et al. Insomnia and the risk of hypertension: A meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. Sleep Med Rev. 2021;56:101403. PMID 33360604. doi:10.1016/j.smrv.2020.101403.

rows.sourceTitle: Periodontitis and risk of immune-mediated systemic conditions: A systematic review and meta-analysis
rows.sourceType: systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies
rows.proposition: Longitudinal evidence found increased incident osteoporosis risk among people with periodontitis versus controls (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.12-1.75).
rows.phenotypeRestriction: clinically established periodontitis rather than nonspecific periodontal disease; osteoporosis separately diagnosed
rows.publicationGuard: Require periodontitis as the primary phenotype and separately diagnosed osteoporosis. Treat as longitudinal population-level risk/association only. Preserve age, sex/menopause, smoking, glucocorticoid exposure, nutritional status, endocrine disease, immobility, medications and other osteoporosis risks.
rows.citation: Larvin H, Kang J, Aggarwal VR, Pavitt S, Wu J. Periodontitis and risk of immune-mediated systemic conditions: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Community Dent Oral Epidemiol. 2023;51(5):705-717. PMID 36377800. doi:10.1111/cdoe.12812.
rows.evidenceType: systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies

rows.sourceTitle: Unexpected coexistent endometriosis in women with symptomatic uterine leiomyomas is independently associated with infertility, nulliparity and minor myoma size
rows.proposition: Among women undergoing laparoscopic myomectomy for symptomatic leiomyomas, 25.6% had unexpected histologically confirmed endometriosis, supporting clinically relevant co-occurrence.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: symptomatic uterine leiomyomas/fibroids with separately diagnosed endometriosis
rows.publicationGuard: Treat strictly as co-occurrence/association and screening relevance, not fibroids causing endometriosis. Preserve shared estrogen-related biology, age, infertility/nulliparity, referral and surgical-selection bias, and other endometriosis risk factors.
rows.citation: Nicolaus K, Bräuer D, Sczesny R, Lehmann T, Diebolder H, Runnebaum IB. Unexpected coexistent endometriosis in women with symptomatic uterine leiomyomas is independently associated with infertility, nulliparity and minor myoma size. Arch Gynecol Obstet. 2019;300(1):103-108. PMID 31006843. doi:10.1007/s00404-019-05153-5.

rows.sourceTitle: Pulmonary hypertension following lung transplant: a systematic review
rows.sourceType: systematic review (12 case reports + 3 retrospective cohort studies; 223 patients)
rows.proposition: In lung-transplant recipients with post-transplant pulmonary hypertension, chronic lung allograft dysfunction—particularly bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome—was the most frequently reported etiology/association, accounting for 63% of included cases.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: post-lung-transplant bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome/chronic lung allograft dysfunction; pulmonary hypertension separately diagnosed
rows.publicationGuard: Use only for bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome/chronic lung allograft dysfunction after lung transplantation, with separately diagnosed pulmonary hypertension. Do not generalize to ordinary acute bronchiolitis. Preserve vascular/anastomotic complications, recurrent idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension, recurrent thromboembolic disease, left-heart/diastolic dysfunction, underlying transplant indication and other pulmonary-hypertension causes. The review calls for prospective longitudinal studies; do not state individual causation.
rows.citation: Bachar R, Tager D, Berro J, Nero N, Sehgal S, Mehta AC. Pulmonary hypertension following lung transplant: a systematic review. J Thorac Dis. 2026;18(6):685. PMID 42444963. doi:10.21037/jtd-2026-0713.
rows.evidenceType: systematic review (12 case reports + 3 retrospective cohort studies; 223 patients)
